---
title: "PMFGLM.jl"
---

Single-node primordial magnetic-field simulations with full GLM magnetohydrodynamics,
particle gravity, photon-baryon response, and primordial chemistry. Julia and
KernelAbstractions share the numerical kernels across parallel CPU, Apple Metal,
and NVIDIA CUDA. The package bundles its source dependencies; no Vespa checkout,
private registry, or sibling science repository is required.

## Start here {#sec-start}

```sh
git clone https://github.com/yipihey/pmf-glm.git
cd pmf-glm
julia --project=. -t auto scripts/bootstrap.jl --backend=cpu
julia --project=. -t auto scripts/run_pmf.jl examples/smoke.toml \
  --output=results/first --backend=cpu
```

The [installation guide](getting-started.qmd) targets a first small CPU run in
about five minutes after Julia is installed; dependency downloads and first
compilation can take longer. For Apple Silicon or NVIDIA, follow the separate
[GPU setup](backends.qmd) before changing the backend.

## Scope {#sec-scope}

The research runner retains nonlinear finite-volume MHD throughout radiation
coupling. The photon model evolves a monopole and velocity with an algebraic
stress closure: it is **not a full polarized Boltzmann hierarchy**. Gaussian
Lyman-alpha mixing and response-table chemistry are model approximations, not
three-dimensional line radiative transfer. See the [science boundary](validation.qmd#sec-limitations).

::: {.callout-warning}
## Evidence belongs to a revision
Inherited tests, historical Metal runs, and Schiff comparison tools describe
lineage, not certification of this extraction. CUDA support in the source does
not establish CUDA hardware validation. Only the [evidence page](test-results.qmd)
reports measurements supplied with this documentation build.
:::

## Package surface {#sec-package-surface}

The public facade exposes configuration and run orchestration, plus selected MHD
operations. The bundled `MHDKernels`, `PoissonKernels`, `ChemistryKernels`, and
`EmissionKernels` remain accessible through `PMFGLM`.
{{< src "src/PMFGLM.jl" "module PMFGLM" >}}

```julia
using PMFGLM
config = load_config("examples/cosmology-smoke.toml")
resolved = run_environment(config; output_dir="results/inspect")
run_simulation(config; output_dir="results/cosmology-first")
```

Use a new directory per experiment. The runner records the resolved options,
source fingerprint, dependency-manifest hash, execution log, and completion
status. A completed short run is an installation check, not a convergence result.
